problem: The new except branch passes the HMAC signing key SECRET_KEY to log.exception with %r. Any signing failure writes the secret to every configured log handler in plaintext.
failure: With SECRET_KEY=topsecret set, call sign("abc") with a str instead of bytes. hmac raises TypeError, and the ERROR log record reads "signing failed, key='topsecret' payload='abc'" along with the traceback. Anyone who can read the logs can then forge signatures.
fix: Remove the try/except and go back to the single-line return. If a log line is required, leave out the key entirely.

problem: The same log call writes the full payload being signed with %r. Session tokens or PII passed to sign() end up in logs at ERROR level whenever signing fails.
failure: Call sign() on a payload of an unsupported type, such as a dict holding a session token. The log record contains payload={...token...} in plaintext.
fix: Do not log the payload. At most, log type(payload).__name__ and its length.

problem: SECRET_KEY.encode() now runs inside the try. If encoding the key itself fails, the handler catches that and logs the raw key, so a bad config value also leaks the secret.
failure: Set SECRET_KEY to a value with lone surrogates, for example from non-UTF-8 environment bytes decoded with surrogateescape. Calling sign(b"x") raises UnicodeEncodeError, and the handler logs key='<raw secret>'.
fix: Remove the try/except, or encode the key outside the try and never log it.
